judge_assessment.explanation: Every mathematical claim the judge made checks out. I re-derived all ten items from worksheet.pdf and verify.json: dV/dt = 4*pi*25*2 = 200*pi (id 3); dy/dt = -(5/12)*4 = -5/3 with y = 12 recovered from 13^2 - 5^2 (id 6); V'(x) = 12(x-2)(x-6) so V(2) = 2*8^2 = 128 in^3 (id 7); dh/dt = 4*9/(pi*36) = 1/pi ft/min (id 9); A'(x) = 18 - 6x^2 gives x = sqrt(3) and A(sqrt(3)) = 12*sqrt(3) (id 10). The counts are right too: ten problems, warm-up at 1, synthesis at 10, and the three strands really do rotate (curve analysis 1/2/5/8, related rates 3/6/9, optimization 4/7/10). What the judge did not do is open final_response.md against references/standards-map.md, or check that every printed answer slot has a verify entry, and both fail. (1) final_response.md's closing section asserts that standards-map.md has 'no row for the analytical-applications unit that covers increasing/decreasing, concavity and inflection (FUN-4.A)'. Line 135 of references/standards-map.md is verbatim '| Analytical applications (increasing/decreasing, concavity, inflection) | FUN-4.A |'. The row exists; the claim is false, and the delivered answer_key.pdf's Curriculum block then prints 'FUN-4.B-FUN-4.C - problems 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 10', tagging the increasing-interval item (2), the concavity/inflection item (5) and the extrema-analysis item (8) with the Optimization code. (2) Problem 2 prints one 'Answer:' slot for two demands - 'find every critical number of f, and state on which intervals f is increasing'. verify.json id 2 is a single solve of 3x^2-12x+9 = [1,3]; the increasing intervals (-inf,1) and (3,inf), which the key spends its whole Step 4 on, are not in the verified data. (3) Problem 5 asks the student to 'decide which of them are inflection points of f and justify your decision', problem 6 asks 'say what the sign means', and problem 7(a) asks 'say which one the domain rejects and why'. All three are written judgments and none has a manual companion entry, even though this very file shows the pattern is available - problem 10 carries a solve entry and a separate {"type":"manual"} entry under the same id.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 7 is built so that the wrong answer is the lesson: V'(x) = 12(x-2)(x-6) has a root at x = 6 that the physical domain 0 < x < 6 forbids, the worksheet explicitly asks 'which one the domain rejects and why', and the key's grading note says 'an answer of x = 6 is the whole point of the problem - the algebra is right and the model is not'. That is a domain check taught as a habit rather than mentioned as a caveat.

The key's problem 5 Step 4 does not stop at 'both are inflection points'; it adds the g(x) = x^4 counterexample where g''(0) = 0 but the concavity never changes, and then says 'That is why Step 4 exists'. The necessary-versus-sufficient distinction is the actual assessed idea and the key names it.

Both declared traps are derived expressions rather than typed numbers: id 3's trap is 4*pi*r**2 (the surface area you get by dropping dr/dt) and id 9's is k/(pi*h**2) (the cross-section you get by skipping r = h/2). Each reproduces a specific wrong method, and the key prints the diagnosis beside the number.

root_causes.description: The delivery step narrates a standards-map gap instead of reading the map. final_response.md claims FUN-4.A has no row when line 135 of references/standards-map.md carries it, and the answer key's Curriculum block consequently prints the Optimization code FUN-4.B-FUN-4.C on the three curve-analysis problems (2, 5, 8).
evidence: references/standards-map.md line 135: '| Analytical applications (increasing/decreasing, concavity, inflection) | FUN-4.A |'
final_response.md: 'no row for the analytical-applications unit that covers increasing/decreasing, concavity and inflection (FUN-4.A)'

root_causes.description: Verification covers the computational half of each problem and silently drops the interpretive half. Problem 2's increasing intervals have no entry at all; problems 5, 6 and 7(a) each demand a written justification that is recorded under a machine-verified type with no manual companion, so gate_log.txt reports 14 machine-verified checks and exactly one manual item when four items carry open reasoning.
evidence: worksheet.pdf problem 2: 'find every critical number of f, and state on which intervals f is increasing' - verify.json id 2 is only {"type":"solve","expr":"3*x**2 - 12*x + 9","expected":[1,3]}
worksheet.pdf problem 5: 'decide which of them are inflection points of f and justify your decision' - verify.json id 5 is a lone solve of 12*x**2 - 24*x
verify.json id 10 shows the two-entry pattern (solve + manual under one id) that ids 2, 5, 6 and 7 needed and did not get

improvements.title: Grep references/standards-map.md before claiming a strand has no code, and tag curve analysis FUN-4.A
improvements.proposed_change: Make the standards step a lookup, not a recollection. In SKILL.md's tagging instructions, require that any sentence of the form 'standards-map.md has no row for X' be preceded by an actual search of references/standards-map.md, and that the search result be quoted. Add a build-time check that scans final_response.md for the phrases 'no row', 'no entry' and 'no code' near a standards reference and fails the gate unless the named code is genuinely absent from references/standards-map.md. For this case the fix is one line: tag problems 2, 5 and 8 FUN-4.A (Analytical applications) rather than FUN-4.B-FUN-4.C (Optimization), leaving 4, 7 and 10 on the optimization code.
improvements.regression_test: Add a fixture whose final_response.md contains 'standards-map.md has no row for FUN-4.A' together with references/standards-map.md line 135. The new checker must exit non-zero with a message naming line 135. Before the fix the checker does not exist and the build passes; after it, this fixture fails and a control fixture claiming a genuinely absent code still passes.
improvements.expected_impact: Curve-analysis problems carry the code that actually describes them, and the whole class of 'the map has no entry, so I substituted a different code' claims (curr-301, curr-312, curr-345, curr-351, curr-373 and this case) stops reaching delivery.
improvements.risk: Low. The checker only fires on an explicit absence claim, so correctly worded responses are untouched. Slight risk of a false positive if a response discusses a code in prose without asserting absence; the phrase list keeps that narrow.

improvements.title: Problem 2 asks for critical numbers and increasing intervals; only the critical numbers are verified
improvements.proposed_change: Count the demands in each problem stem, not the problems. Have the discovery step split every stem on 'and', 'then' and lettered parts, and require one verify entry (machine or manual) per demand; the gate should fail when a stem contains more imperative verbs than the id has entries. For this worksheet, id 2 needs a companion entry pinning the increasing set - e.g. a solve/compare pair establishing that f' > 0 on (-inf,1) and (3,inf) - and id 5 needs an entry for the inflection-point decision at x = 0 and x = 2.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture: a verify.json whose id 2 stem is 'find every critical number of f, and state on which intervals f is increasing' with a single solve entry. The demand-counting gate must fail with 'problem 2: 2 demands, 1 entry'. Adding the second entry makes it pass. Today the same fixture passes with one entry.
improvements.expected_impact: Removes the largest verification blind spot in this run: the interpretive second half of a two-part stem stops being delivered as 'machine-verified' when nothing checked it.
improvements.risk: Medium. Naive verb counting will over-trigger on stems that use 'and' rhetorically; the splitter needs a tested heuristic plus an explicit per-problem override so authors can record 'one demand' deliberately.

improvements.title: The justification halves of problems 5, 6 and 7 are delivered as machine-verified
improvements.proposed_change: Treat 'justify', 'say what ... means', 'say why', 'explain' and 'decide ... and justify' in a stem as a hard trigger for a manual companion entry under the same id, mirroring what id 10 already does. verify.py should refuse to mark a problem fully machine-verified when its stem carries one of those verbs and the id has no manual entry, and gate_log.txt's manual count should then read 4 for this sheet rather than 1.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture with a stem containing 'justify your decision' and only a solve entry: verify.py must exit with a message requiring a manual companion. The same fixture with a manual entry added under the same id passes. Currently the first form passes clean.
improvements.expected_impact: The manual-review count in the final response becomes an honest description of what a teacher still has to read, and open reasoning stops being covered by the sentence 'machine-verified with SymPy'.
improvements.risk: Low to medium. Some stems say 'show your work' without adding a gradable claim; over-flagging would inflate manual counts, so the verb list should stay short and be fixture-locked.

case_summary: A genuinely strong interleaved derivative-applications sheet: ten problems, three strands rotating after a one-item warm-up, a difficulty ramp from 1 to 5, and an answer key whose Step 1 always names why a particular tool applies. I recomputed every number the judge cited and all of them are correct, as are the two declared traps, which are expressions derived from named wrong methods rather than typed values. Two defects the judge did not reach. First, final_response.md asserts that references/standards-map.md has no FUN-4.A row when line 135 carries it verbatim, and the delivered key then tags the three curve-analysis problems (2, 5, 8) with the Optimization code FUN-4.B-FUN-4.C. Second, the verification contract covers only the computational half of several items: problem 2's increasing intervals have no entry at all, and the justification demands in problems 5, 6 and 7(a) are delivered inside machine-verified ids even though the file demonstrates the correct two-entry pattern at problem 10. Page counts in the final response match the built PDFs (worksheet 6, study guide 2), the study guide teaches all three strands with a rule box, a worked example and a distinct try-it, and the layout is clean if spacious at six pages for ten problems.
